title: runtime/scheduler: classify requests as short/long using prompt length + optional prefill cost predictor
author: Marcus Reed
description: Context: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (ENG-2417) needs a stable, cheap way to bucket incoming generation requests into latency-sensitive "short" vs throughput-oriented "long" before we apply any two-queue dispatch policy (PR to follow). Problem: The existing continuous batching queue treats all prefills equally; under mixed prompt distributions long-context prefills can dominate selection and inflate tail latency. This PR introduces request classification logic + config plumbing + unit tests. Approach: We classify each request at enqueue time based on (a) prompt/context tokens and (b) an optional predicted prefill cost estimate (enabled via config). The default behavior is prompt token threshold only to keep this safe for early canaries. The cost predictor is intentionally simple (linear model over prompt tokens + attention kv factors) and can be swapped later. Changes: (1) Add SchedulerClass enum { SHORT, LONG } stored on RequestContext (derived at admission). (2) Add config knobs under scheduler.classification.*: enabled, mode=[prompt_tokens|prefill_cost|hybrid], short_max_prompt_tokens, short_max_prefill_cost, long_force_prompt_tokens, min_tokens_for_cost_model, and validation bounds. (3) Add a small helper to compute prompt_tokens consistently (accounts for cached prefix tokens when prefix caching is enabled). (4) Add unit tests for boundary behavior, cached-prefix interactions, and config validation; include one regression test from SUP-19387 reproduction where long-context load causes TTFT regression if long requests are misclassified as short. Notes: This PR only labels requests and emits debug counters; it does not yet change dispatch behavior. Follow-up PR (24844) will consume SchedulerClass for two-queue selection + aging. Risk: misclassification could shift load between queues in future work; we gate this with feature flag and conservative defaults. Rollout: default disabled in all pools; enabled only in benchmark-lab/perf-canary via explicit config. Observability: adds lightweight counters for class distribution and "unclassified"/fallback cases; full per-class latency metrics come in later instrumentation PR.
commits: runtime/scheduler: introduce SchedulerClass + classification hook at enqueue
runtime: compute prompt_tokens using effective_context_tokens (prefix cache aware)
tests: add classification unit tests + cached-prefix edge cases
docs: add internal comments + config examples for benchmark harness
notable_snippet: Pseudo-code (from runtime/scheduler/classification.cc): if (!cfg.enabled) return SchedulerClass::SHORT; // legacy single-queue behavior. auto prompt = effective_prompt_tokens(req, cache_state); switch (cfg.mode) { case PROMPT_TOKENS: return (prompt <= cfg.short_max_prompt_tokens) ? SHORT : LONG; case PREFILL_COST: return (predict_prefill_cost(prompt, cfg) <= cfg.short_max_prefill_cost) ? SHORT : LONG; case HYBRID: if (prompt >= cfg.long_force_prompt_tokens) return LONG; auto cost = predict_prefill_cost(prompt, cfg); return (prompt <= cfg.short_max_prompt_tokens && cost <= cfg.short_max_prefill_cost) ? SHORT : LONG; }
review_conversation: Lena Fischer: Can we make sure the default when disabled is identical to existing behavior? I don't want a hidden behavior change before 24844 lands.

Marcus Reed (author): Yep. When classification is disabled we return SHORT unconditionally and do not change queue selection. Added test "DisabledClassification_IsNoop" to assert the scheduler still exposes a single queue path.

Omar El-Sayed: effective_prompt_tokens() needs to account for prefix cache hits; otherwise a request with cached prefix could be mislabeled as long and hurt throughput when we add queueing. Can you wire in the cache state?
Marcus Reed (author): Done. effective_prompt_tokens() subtracts cached_prefix_tokens when prefix caching is enabled + hit is present. Added tests for {no cache, partial hit, full hit}.
Yuki Sato: Cost model: please keep it behind config and deterministic. Also, can we clamp the inputs so we don't overflow when prompt_tokens is huge?

Marcus Reed (author): Cost model stays off by default and is a simple linear estimate with clamps. Added validation: prompt_tokens capped at 1,048,576 for prediction; also added cfg bounds for thresholds.
Allison Grant: Metrics naming: please align counters with our conventions (snake_case, unit suffix if applicable). Also make sure labels are limited.
Marcus Reed (author): Updated to scheduler_classification_requests_total{class=short|long|fallback} and scheduler_classification_fallback_total{reason=...}. No high-cardinality labels.
Lena Fischer: Looks good. Please add a short note in the description that this PR doesn't implement two-queue, only classification.
Marcus Reed (author): Added to description + included follow-up pointer to 24844.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Connor O'Brien. Squash commit: 9f3c2d1 runtime/scheduler: add short/long classification + config knobs.
release_notes: Internal-only: adds request classification plumbing (short vs long) behind scheduler.classification.enabled; no behavior change unless explicitly enabled via config.
